Evidence needed: an owner ruling, in the same form as UNK-0004 (an accepted, named deviation) if mirroring is chosen.

[PROVCLI] UNK-0006, PR-PROVCLI-203: Command Code's executable name is the bare `cmd`. On Windows, PATH plus PATHEXT resolution finds C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe long before any provider CLI, and launching it with this provider's argv opens a console that speaks no protocol, so the session hangs at the first read. Missing evidence: (a) which identity signal distinguishes the provider from the interpreter - resolved path, file version information, or a handshake the interpreter cannot answer; (b) where the CLI actually installs on Windows, since the five fallback directories in the source are entirely macOS and Unix package-manager paths. Both need a Windows probe. No executable name or directory may be hard-coded for this provider until they are settled.

[PROVCLI] UNK-0006, PR-PROVCLI-240 and PR-PROVCLI-256: several Command Code user-visible strings instruct the user to run `cmd login` in Terminal. Whether that is the correct instruction for the Windows CLI depends on the same unresolved identity and install question. The strings are specified verbatim and must NOT be reworded without that evidence.

[PROVCLI] UNK-0005, PR-PROVCLI-247 and PR-PROVCLI-305: two gates classify model-issued command TEXT to decide whether to auto-approve - ShellCommandKind.mayWriteFiles for Command Code's Auto mode, and the Pi extension's own isReadOnlyCommand over an 18-binary and 6-git-subcommand list. Both lists are product constants applied to text the model produced, so they port verbatim. What is NOT in source is what shell each CLI runs that text in on Windows. If a Windows-hosted CLI emits Windows command text, both classifiers simply fail to recognize it and ask the user more often, which is safe - but that is a behavioural change in frequency and must be measured, not assumed.

[PROVCLI] PR-PROVCLI-254: the shipped Command Code mod's orphan test is `process.ppid === 1`, which is a POSIX idiom with no Windows meaning. On Windows it never fires, so a gate stranded by an app crash waits the full six hours rather than giving up. Missing evidence: what process.ppid actually reports on Windows after the parent exits. Editing the shipped TypeScript is a product change to a security-relevant gate and is not made without a decision.

[PROVCLI] PR-PROVCLI-213, PR-PROVCLI-252, PR-PROVCLI-269, PR-PROVCLI-302: four paths hand a Windows filesystem path to a CLI that will load it as a module - Command Code's `--mod <path>` and its bridge dynamic import, and Pi's `-e <path>` and its bridge dynamic import. Whether each accepts a bare Windows path or requires a file URL is not in source and must be probed against the real CLIs.

[PROVCLI] PR-PROVCLI-219, PR-PROVCLI-236, PR-PROVCLI-238: Command Code keys an interrupted turn on exit code 130, the POSIX SIGINT convention, which does not arise on Windows. The interruptRequested flag carries the behavior, so the 130 test must be relaxed - but the Windows termination exit code must be chosen deliberately so it does not collide with the CLI's own meaningful codes 3 through 10.

[PROVCLI] PR-PROVCLI-207 and PR-PROVCLI-268: CommandCodeAPI interpolates AppInfo.name into its support directory while PiCLI hard-codes the literal "Droppy Code/pi". A build whose display name differs scatters helper files across two roots, and the Pi path is handed to the CLI at launch. Recorded as upstream defect 8; the resolution is deliberate, not automatic, and is entangled with the product-identity decision in UNK-0002.

[PROVCLI] PR-PROVCLI-260 and PR-PROVCLI-338: two catalogs are parsed out of printed console output - Command Code's two-or-more-space column split and Antigravity's TAB-separated rows. Both depend on how the CLI formats for a pipe on Windows. Neither can be called verified until the real output is captured on Windows; the parsers are specified from source, the Windows fidelity is not asserted.

[PROVCLI] PR-PROVCLI-011 and PR-PROVCLI-136: Claude's --agents and Copilot's --additional-mcp-config each pass a whole JSON document as ONE argv token. Windows caps a command line at 32767 characters and its quoting rules interact badly with embedded quotes and trailing backslashes. Whether the largest realistic Hydra configuration and MCP config fit, and survive quoting byte-identically, must be measured rather than assumed.

[PROVCLI] PR-PROVCLI-178: Copilot de-duplicates reasoning text by Swift hashValue, which is randomly seeded per process. Stability within one run is required and cross-run stability is not relied on; the port must not turn it into a persisted key. A hash collision silently suppressing a distinct reasoning text is upstream behavior.

[PROVACP] Windows path relativization is a real platform boundary I could not settle from macOS source alone. ToolTitles.relativePath (ProviderSession.swift:188-191) appends a forward slash to the working directory and does a case-sensitive prefix compare. On Windows the four agent CLIs will report backslash paths, and Windows paths are case-insensitive, so the same comparison can fail where macOS succeeds and leave absolute paths in tool row titles. Missing evidence: what each of cursor-agent, opencode, grok and devin actually emits for locations[].path and rawInput.filePath on Windows, including drive-letter casing and whether any of them normalizes to forward slashes. This must be probed against the real CLIs, not guessed. Specified as PR-PROVACP-119 with the boundary named.

[PROVACP] ToolTitles.unwrapShell (ProviderSession.swift:174-186) strips exactly six Unix shell prefixes (/bin/zsh -lc, /bin/bash -lc, bash -lc, zsh -lc, /bin/sh -c, sh -c). On Windows an agent CLI is likely to report a bare command or a cmd.exe or powershell wrapper, none of which are in the list, so such a command row shows the wrapper text. I specified reproducing the six-entry list verbatim and explicitly did NOT add Windows shell prefixes, because that would be an invented default. Missing evidence: the actual command strings each of the four CLIs reports on Windows. Record those before proposing any change.

[PROVACP] port_impacts.md entry 18 states that on Windows the lines framer must tolerate a trailing 0x0D reaching the JSON parser 'because the source does not strip CR'. That is true of StdioFramer (StdioFramer.swift:26-34 splits on 0x0A only) but NOT of StdioProcess.deliver (StdioProcess.swift:145), which strips trailing 0x0D and 0x20 before parsing. The practical claim in that impact entry is therefore wrong: CR never reaches the parser. I specified the source behavior (PR-PROVACP-149 and PR-PROVACP-155) and flagged the discrepancy in both rows. The impact entry should be corrected rather than implemented as written.

[PROVACP] StdioProcess.terminate kills the child pid only, not the process group (StdioProcess.swift:121), unlike Shell.swift which PA-0007 describes as killing the group via a negative pid. A grandchild - most plausibly the npx mcp-remote process an agent spawns when the agent does not speak HTTP MCP - therefore survives on macOS, and will equally survive on Windows where there is no process-group cleanup at all. I specified reproducing the pid-only kill (PR-PROVACP-157) and explicitly ruled out introducing a Job Object group kill here, because that would change observable behavior. Missing evidence: whether an orphaned npx/node grandchild on Windows holds the agent's stdout handle long enough to matter beyond the 1-second forced close at StdioProcess.swift:175-178. Needs a run, not a read. This is also a Gate E child-process-cleanup item.

[PROVACP] StdioProcess.terminate's three-second graceful window has no real Windows equivalent: TerminateProcess behaves like SIGKILL, so the first step is already forceful and the second is redundant. I specified preserving the ordering and the 3-second timing anyway (PR-PROVACP-157) so that a CLI which would have flushed on SIGTERM is not observably different in timing. Missing evidence: whether any of the four CLIs actually does anything on SIGTERM on macOS. If none does, the Windows collapse is unobservable and the 3-second wait could be reconsidered - but only with that evidence in hand.
